## Scope, levels and environment

One student implements and verifies; the owner resolves policy and evaluates criteria. The release gate contains 60 Must requirements under ADR-0010. FR-45 is Withdrawn, not renumbered; FR-35 remains Enhanced/Won't. Seven named original Core exceptions remain optional for this release, without reducing the other Musts. No automatic additional cut is permitted.

Runnable context/contract-definition and diagram checks exist. Real PostgreSQL storage migrations and synthetic database tests also exist: the latest recorded database run passed 12 results (11 scenarios plus parent). These verify storage prerequisites, not full feature ACs, application authentication/permission, transport concurrency or provider quality. Application handlers, end-to-end UI tests and model evaluation remain unimplemented/unrun. Five guard tests are TODO declarations, not passes.

Use unit tests for domain transitions and evidence binding; owning-database integration tests for transactions/constraints; consumer-provider tests for service identity, authority and failure semantics; system/UI tests for complete user actions, refresh/resync and accessible interaction; manual evaluation for claim support and usability. Do not infer one level's result from another.

Target test environment: two isolated owned databases, Workspace permission gateway, Knowledge process and controllable provider/transport adapters. ## Coverage and execution order

Read [TEST-COVERAGE-01](test-coverage.md): all eight SCs and BR-01-BR-14 have named gates. The UC matrix retains 49 named EX identities: 48 active and one Withdrawn. Inventory completeness is not implementation or runtime coverage.

Begin audit capture with the first mutation. For every test record actor/capability scope, snapshot/configuration, request/key/revision, controlled pause/commit/handoff boundary, persisted state and observed response/transport. TC-26 now uses manifest-bound ProviderInput and InternalQuestionResult. TC-08: change current blocker/task state after an operational citation was delivered; open its observation locator, fetch exact current entity under renewed project scope and label the two separately. Denial must not repopulate cached titles/current values or call a document citation endpoint. No historical snapshot read is invented.

TC-10/22: terminal AI failure followed by deliberate new request and success clears stale health/error UI; no background loop. Lose a response and verify explicit unknown state, no automatic replay/new-ID resend and server quarantine respected by any new user request. Test expired session and membership loss separately from provider recovery. TC-20: semantic pending/failed plus committed permitted Current passages still allows keyword results; Current alone promises neither path. These are planned runtime/UI cases; contract negatives only protect explicit semantic readiness fields.

## NEXT-06 command precondition and receipt scenarios

TC-03/05/06/13/20: revoke restricted-author read but retain exact write/lifecycle authority; deny all content/history/readiness while allowing known-ID opaque precondition and new-text revision/archive/delete. Return only minimal receipt, never Version/Document content. Read-only/manage-only actor is denied the requested command precondition. Race revocation/session change and revision; reject wrong actor/project/document/action/version/generation and stale/unknown tokens without current revision/state leakage. Commit state/audit/token consumption atomically, roll back all on failure and return original minimal same-key receipt without re-executing or requiring a consumed token. A changed replay payload conflicts. Unknown outcome keeps the original key; a new precondition does not prove rollback. FR-65 remains Could. Contract negatives cover selected precondition unions and receipt disclosure only; runtime/SQL tests are unrun.

## NEXT-07 contract example checks

`npm run contracts:test` evaluates synthetic component-schema samples with pinned development tooling after `npm ci`. It compiles the current OpenAPI component schemas and checks valid/invalid metric states, inspection locators, full version discovery identity, command selector exclusivity, minimal acknowledgements and manifest purposes. Inputs are never coerced, defaulted or stripped. This supplements declaration checks; it neither validates the complete OpenAPI document nor executes HTTP, permissions, storage, relay or UI behavior. Non-schema semantics in TC-26 and command/token/reorder scenarios remain unrun.

## NEXT-08 document and inline-schema checks

The same contract test command now adds whole-document structure checks using the pinned official 3.1.x schema and a calibrated local dynamic-reference specialization. Schema Object validation remains a separate JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-validation/compilation step for both named components and inline HTTP schemas. A valid synthetic document and malformed response/parameter/operation cases calibrate the structure adapter; an invalid inline schema must fail while arbitrary example data stays opaque. Source hash and license are recorded under tests/fixtures/openapi31. This is bounded structural evidence, without document-level format assertions, external dialect overrides, full standard semantics or live HTTP acceptance.

## NEXT-09 operational inspector reload scenario

TC-08 / NFR-01: deliver an operational citation, open its inspector, then reload/direct-navigate after losing the original answer context. The historical panel must state original cited observation unavailable; a renewed current entity read is separate and cannot supply historical observation time/revision/value. Tampered URL observation parameters or browser storage must not become authoritative history. Back navigation may retain actual in-memory delivered context but still renews scope; denied/expired scope clears protected details. Do not auto-submit a new question or borrow trace/optional-summary entitlement. These are planned UI assertions; no browser handler/prototype test ran in this textual correction.

## NEXT-10 routing/authentication declaration regressions

Dependency-free context tests now reject empty or partial authentication alternatives for all eight actual internal operations, public session opt-outs/unknown schemes, duplicate/extra/missing path parameters and equivalent templated routes. Positive tests retain inherited parameter references and legal operation overrides; cyclic references fail, and HEAD cannot bypass requirement trace. This tests the harness through current full contracts. Real HTTP authentication, guard and route behavior remain Not run.

## NEXT-11 executable byte reference for TC-26

HANDOFF-REF-01 adds local tests for canonical base64, byte limits, invalid UTF-8/JSON/decoded duplicate keys, exact integers, raw byte digest/length, independent preparation/identity, full uncited mixed evidence and exact answer citations/claim references. Whitespace/Unicode changes and UTF-16 versus UTF-8 byte counting are explicit negatives. Zero-evidence insufficiency is retained. The source/capture/receipt fixtures are synthetic test oracles, not real authoritative persistence or access evidence. Provider wire mapping, actual guard/claim/byte boundaries and factual support remain unrun; TC-26 is not Passed.

## NEXT-12 isolated SQL evidence and remaining TC-26

The separate handoff storage suite passed 11 results (10 subtests plus parent), and the updated existing storage suite passed 15 (14 plus parent) on PostgreSQL 17.10 / pgvector 0.8.2. It checks new migration repeat/empty reverse, exact byte/digest/owned identity, rejected malformed/partial metadata and duplicate sources, rollback/append-only rights, both purposes, permanent duplicate claims, two-session claim race, outcome-fence FK, nonempty down refusal and legacy protected-row rejection without mutation. The existing policy/revision/location/retrieval/isolation tests remain passing. All fixtures ran in unique disposable containers; no development migration occurred.

These are SQL service-role/storage tests. Active process fencing, durable/unknown acknowledgements at application boundaries, real scoped getHandoffManifest, source capture/revocation, guard retention, actual provider/answer zero-byte rejection and no automatic resend still need handler/transport evidence. No SP or TC-26 is marked Passed.

## NEXT-13 optional SQL/reference integration

The actual contracts:storage:test command passed seven results (six subtests plus parent) in a fresh isolated container. Both purposes retain exact raw bytes through a canonical StoredHandoff projection. Every trusted-context selector mismatch/NULL yields no row; wrapped base64 and reserialized bytes fail; readable consumed preparations do not regain a claim; a separate connection cannot see uncommitted preparation and cancelled rollback leaves none; unsafe integer parsing fails closed. These are storage/serialization tests with synthetic context, not current permission or HTTP consumer/provider acceptance. No live TC-26 or SP Done is claimed.

## Input metadata reconciliation — 25 October 2026

Only input-version metadata is synchronized for the bounded architecture/UC/checklist corrections. Requirements, acceptance assertions, design body and prior observations are unchanged; no complete semantic review or runtime check is implied.

## P10 input metadata — 28 October 2026

Input versions synchronize the bounded session lifecycle update. Existing requirement, evaluation and UI assertions remain unchanged; no runtime acceptance is inferred from this metadata revision.

## SP-02 measured subset — 1 November 2026

The registered SP-02 execution report maps current create/project/member/replay/discovery/removal/audit/failure checks to AC-02/03/38/39. These include actual disposable 008 PostgreSQL, HTTP, DOM/HTTPS and isolated Edge tests. TC-02/18/22/24 have measured bounded subsets, not whole-case acceptance. SP02-F01 actual future producer races, Knowledge/source/citation/provider and D-07 remain unrun. The original 006 storage/session suites retain explicit schema ceilings; new SP-02 suites exercise 007/008. No threshold, expected outcome or future required assertion is removed.

## SP-03 bounded execution trace — 2 November 2026

[SP-03 execution report](reports/SP-03-2026-11-02-execution.md), [UI report](reports/SP-03-2026-11-02-ui.md) and [registered plan](../implementation/features/sp-03-create-task/plan.md) distinguish source/SQL/HTTP/DOM/browser results and preserve failures. Current final counts belong to that report, not an inferred completion from this design matrix.

| Required creation assertion | Producer and evidence boundary |
| --- | --- |
| AC-05 supported Story/Task/Bug content persists | P04 real Task HTTP + P08 DOM/Edge + P09 fresh current regression; stable ID/project, todo, null assignee, unblocked revision 1 and server time. |
| AC-05 unsupported/invalid content makes no item | P04 invalid body/type/blank/title/extra identity/media/body-size matrix checks Task/generation/audit/outcome unchanged. |

| TC-18/19/22 replay, rollback, unknown outcome and outage | P03B/P04/P07 actual durable outcomes, loss after committed response, exact key/hash recovery, rollback/barriers; P06/P08 unknown/denied/outage UI. |
| Current Backlog reconstruction and permission-aware reads | P05 107-row numeric/UUID/current-location/blocker/cursor/member tests; P07 read watermark/append schedule; P08 fresh first-page restart. |

UC-03 EX-01 and EX-02 now have bounded creation evidence. EX-03/Alt-1 editing and Alt-2 reorder remain later SP-04/SP-05 scope. FR-50 is document classification, not Task creation. # UI/UX and web frontend design blueprint

**Artifact ID:** UX-BLUEPRINT-01  
**Version/date:** 1.7 Draft · 1 November 2026
**Status:** Corrected author draft for bounded wireframe/design work; visual tokens remain candidates. Not owner approval, independent review or application readiness.  
**Template basis:** Local IEEE 1016-2009 Blueprint and UI/UX prompts/checklists; no standards-conformance claim.  
**Inputs:** [PRD-01 v0.9](PRD_SRS.md); [UC-02 v0.8](use-cases.md); [SAD-03 v0.16](../architecture.md); [UX-06 v0.13](ui-ux-spec.md); [UX-CHECK-01 v0.2](reviews/ui-ux-checklist-review-2026-10-18.md); [UX-HANDOFF-01 v0.9](handoffs/ui-ux-handoff-2026-10-18.md); [UX-PLAN-01 v0.4](../ux/wireframe-workplan.md); Workspace OpenAPI v0.2.8; Knowledge OpenAPI v0.2.9; Logical Data Model v0.8; ADR-0004; ADR-0007–ADR-0017; Proposed ADR-0018–ADR-0023; [BRD English v1.0](../baseline/BRD_Scrum_Workspace_AI_KMS_EN_v1.0.md); [PLAN-01 v0.4](../planning/five-month-plan.md); [Stage 6 profile](../agents/06-ui-ux.md); [SP-01 v0.5](../../specs/001-session.md).
**Trace:** BR-01–BR-14; SC-01–SC-08; NFR-01–NFR-09 through PRD/Test Plan; Blueprint B02–B20 and UI/UX U02–U23.

## 1. Context and subject

### 1.1 Identification and authority

Scrum Workspace with AI-Assisted Knowledge Management System (KMS), UI/UX design v1.3 Draft, 23 October 2026. Author role: Stage 6 UI/UX author. This document translates UX-06 into screen, component and interaction briefs. UX-06 remains the consolidated entry; SAD, PRD and contracts remain their canonical sources. Templates and author proposals cannot change product scope or select a framework/provider.

#### Revision History

| Version | Date | Author | Description of Changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1 | 2026-10-18 | UI/UX Author | Initial checklist analysis and handoff boundaries (UX-CHECK-01, UX-HANDOFF-01). |
| v1.0 | 2026-10-19 | UI/UX Author | Full IEEE 1016-2009 Blueprint creation integrating 8 design views, component catalogs, state dynamics, and complete checklist dispositions. |
| v1.1 | 2026-10-20 | UI/UX Author | Reconciled with upstream SAD-03 gateway boundaries (Trust Boundary 1 & 4), explicit Proposed ADR-0018–0023 labeling, canonical UX-SITEMAP-03 routes, claim-level badges (FR-24), UX constraints matrix completion, and UX-CHECK-01 checklist reconciliation notes. |
| v1.2 | 2026-10-21 | UI/UX Author | Preserved v1.1 gateway/routes; corrected actors, contract bindings, state/trace errors, visual evidence claims and sequential construction briefs. |
| v1.3 | 2026-10-23 | UI/UX Author | Bound task placement to Task.work_location and exposed optional run summary from the answer independently of Audit navigation; existing contracts and Proposed designs unchanged. |


### 1.2 Boundaries

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Browser["Browser presentation UI - apps/web"]
    subgraph Workspace["Workspace service"]
        GW["Authenticated gateway / session context"]
        Work["Projects, Scrum and permission authority"]
        Relay["Guarded provider relay"]
    end
    subgraph Knowledge["Knowledge service"]
        Docs["Immutable documents and versions"]
        Evidence["Keyword/vector retrieval, evidence and citation validation"]
    end
    Provider["Unselected embedding / generation provider"]
    Browser -->|Authenticated public contracts| GW
    GW --> Work
    GW -->|Authenticated internal calls| Docs
    GW -->|Authenticated internal calls| Evidence
    Evidence -.->|Prepared evidence and protected handoff coordination| Relay
    Relay -->|Guarded exact payload transport| Provider
```

Workspace owns permission decisions and provider transport; Knowledge owns documents, retrieval, answer preparation and provenance. Each service writes only its own database. Browser access to Knowledge public paths is proxied/guarded through Workspace; there is no browser/provider or database connection. Internal identity and actor context require service authentication, not an assumed trusted loopback network. Generation waiting is outside the handoff guard. Full evidence-set access/validity checks and frozen-byte handoffs are server responsibilities; UI visibility is not enforcement.

PostgreSQL/pgvector storage is selected under ADR-0004. Application framework, rendering model, identity mechanism, provider and hosting remain open decisions; SAD ports/topology are candidates. Proposed ADR-0018–ADR-0023 supply draft mechanisms, not accepted implementation authority. The v1.1 gateway and canonical sitemap corrections are retained.

### 1.3 Constraints and assumptions

- One student implements the capstone over a relative five-month plan; submission April 2027. Kickoff, weekly capacity and feasibility remain unmeasured. Product actors remain a team with scoped capabilities.
- Retain the original 60 release Must. FR-27/49/62/70 are Should, FR-64–67 Could, FR-35 outside this release, FR-45 Withdrawn. Enhanced reports and Future Work remain excluded.
- Runtime AI is read-only; authorised humans use normal mutations. No saved conversations/answer store, global user directory, role editor, new service or automatic runtime agent is added.
- Provider failure leaves work, documents and keyword operations usable while their own services/current authority are healthy. Knowledge failure affects docs/search; Workspace/authority failure denies affected protected operations. Semantic readiness is separate from keyword availability.
- Desktop-first layouts and smaller inspection viewports are candidates. Browser/device targets, numeric timing/resource/target-size budgets and visual acceptance remain open in WF-09. Previous unvalidated numeric budgets are withdrawn.

## 2. Stakeholders and concerns

### 2.1 Actors and capabilities

Follow BRD §7, PRD §2 and [personas](../ux/personas.md). Personas are synthetic illustrations, not interviewed users. Solo development does not imply a single-user product.

| Responsibility | Primary journey | Authority boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product Owner | Create/order Backlog; find rationale | Accountability does not grant restricted-source read |
| Scrum Master | Sprint lifecycle and blockers | Scoped action authority required |
| Developer / QA | Update work, follow evidence, maintain content | Content-write and content-read are separate |
| Viewer / stakeholder | Inspect permitted project information | No blanket mutation or inspection entitlement |
| Workspace Admin / document access manager | Membership or document policy management | Neither grants blanket restricted reads; membership and document management are separate |
| Audit / trace inspector | Inspect permitted changes or AI execution | Independent audit/trace entitlements; source access separately checked |
| Student developer / evaluator | Implement, review and assess | Development/review responsibilities confer no runtime access |

Current session identifies the actor. Project AND document scopes apply before context/delivery; unknown authority denies. Descriptive Member.role never provisions capabilities. Additional non-read delegation remains OD-02/OD-08. Scoped audit-read may disclose actor/action/entity-ID/time under ADR-0012 while protected title/content/before-after stay redacted; trace-read inherits no such exception.

### 2.2 Concern-to-design mapping

| Concern | Required design response | Views / planned checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CON-01 work/knowledge navigation | Preserve team journeys and exact scoped controls | §3.1/3.2/3.6; WF-01–06 |
| CON-02 evidence integrity | Exact document/version/passage or operational observation; full-evidence server checks | §3.4/3.5/3.7; WF-07 |
| CON-03 outage continuity | Dependency-specific failure and healthy independent fallback | §1.3/3.4/3.7; TC-12 |
| CON-04 fact/synthesis/uncertainty | Claim labels, supported partials, explicit insufficiency/conflict | §3.2/3.6/3.7; TC-04/09/10 |
| CON-05 concurrent writes | Pending/confirmed/rejected/unknown outcomes and same-identity reconciliation | §3.3/3.4/3.8; WF-02/03/05 |
| CON-06 accessible interaction | Labelled keyboard alternatives, focus containment/return, text with colour | §3.6/4.1; WF-09 rendered review pending |

### 2.3 Quality scenarios and constraints

| Scenario | Planned acceptance observation (not measured evidence) |
| --- | --- |
| Complete Backlog reorder | A member gathers one full generation; pending, confirmed receipt, 409 and lost response differ; TC-07/WF-02 inspect BL-01–BL-10. No response-time claim. |
| Keyboard Board and dialogs | A member uses labelled state controls without drag; focus enters/returns meaningfully, remains contained in an open modal and can exit by closing. Rendered checks pending. |
| AI failure | No generated answer on provider/embedding/budget/persistence failure. Preserve safe input and keyword navigation when healthy; authority/Knowledge failure has separate feedback. |
| Citation reload | Without delivered observation context show Original observation unavailable; label a renewed current entity read separately. No reconstruction from URL/cache. |

Native labels, logical focus, visible focus, field-associated errors and status text are design requirements. Empty success differs from failed authority/dependencies; loading cannot display cached protected content before renewed checks. No hidden title/count/cause appears on denial. Destructive actions explain effects and require explicit confirmation; 409 requires reconsideration. Timings, contrast ratios, touch sizes, zoom/overflow, density and device support need actual rendered evidence; no WCAG claim is made here.

## 3. Design views

### 3.1 Composition view

Symbolic modules describe responsibilities, not an adopted UI framework/component library.

| Module | Responsibility | Declared operations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Auth/shell | Session, project context and clearing protected display | signIn, signOut, getSession, listProjects, getAllowedActions |
| Projects/members | Capability-gated creation and membership; no role editor | createProject, getProject, listMembers, addMember, removeMember; optional editProject |
| Backlog/Sprint planning | Work creation/order, fixed lifecycle, independent allocation outcomes | createTask, listTasks, reorderBacklog, createSprint, listSprints, getSprint, listSprintItems, allocateTask, startSprint, completeSprint |
| Board/task | Direct states, assignee, ordered blockers and current placement | getTask, editTask, setTaskState, setAssignee, listBlockerEvents, recordBlocker |
| Documents/history | Read-filtered list, creation, exact versions and readiness | listDocuments, createDocument, getDocument, listVersions, getVersion, getReadiness |
| Independent access/actions | Known-ID policy or non-reading command surface | getDocumentPolicy, listDocumentReadGrants, setClassification, grantDocumentRead, revokeDocumentRead, getAllowedActions, getDocumentCommandPrecondition, reviseDocument, archiveVersion, deleteDocument; optional editDocumentMetadata |
| Search/relationships | Permitted document keyword search and explicit links | keywordSearch, listLinks, createLink; optional searchTasks/removeLink |
| AI/citation inspector | Buffered answer and both citation kinds | askQuestion, openCitation, getVersion; renewed getProject/getSprint/getTask |
| Audit/trace | Separate audit, trace and optional summary authorities | listAudit, getTrace; optional getRetrievalSummary |

Multi-select Sprint allocation is one allocateTask request/key/result per task, not a bulk transaction (ADR-0014). First human work/document journeys precede AI. Keep fixed Planned → Active → Completed Sprint lifecycle, one Active Sprint/project and direct task state transitions.

### 3.2 Logical view

| View model | Contract source / invariant |
| --- | --- |
| Session/project context | Session and exact-scope AllowedActions; descriptive roles grant no authority |
| Work card | Task.state/revision and Task.work_location: kind=backlog uses position; kind=sprint or completed uses sprint_id. These are API fields, not logical-model location_kind/location_sprint_id; completion history cannot derive current placement |
| Document list/history | DocumentSummary/VersionSummary; nullable Current pointer; Current/Superseded/Archived separate from semantic_readiness |
| Answer | QuestionResult union with server-controlled claims, citations and missing_components where applicable |
| Document citation | kind=document, source_id, document_id, version_id, passage_id; no invented offset locator |
| Operational citation | kind=operational, source_id, entity_kind, entity_id, observed_at, observation_revision |
| Command context | Exact action/target, original scoped operation identity/payload and either known revision or opaque precondition_token |

These are UI projections of existing schemas, not alternate HTTP definitions or added fields. Full evidence validity and claim support are distinct from locator structure.

### 3.3 Dependency view

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Views["UI views and interaction state"] --> Adapters["HTTP adapters - framework unselected"]
    Adapters --> Workspace["Workspace public contract v0.2.8"]
    Adapters --> Knowledge["Knowledge public contract v0.2.9 via gateway"]
    Workspace --> Authority["Server current scoped authority"]
    Knowledge --> Authority
```

No copied permission rules or direct DB/provider access. Discovery controls affordances; every server operation rechecks current authority and business preconditions. Failure clears stale allowed actions/protected output; browser caches never become unrestricted fallback. Application stack remains Proposed.

### 3.4 Interaction view

#### 3.4.1 Work mutation

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor Member
    participant UI as Board
    participant GW as Workspace gateway
    Member->>UI: Choose Done with pointer or keyboard
    UI->>UI: Mark pending and preserve original key/payload
    UI->>GW: POST /tasks/{task_id}/state with state=done and expected_revision
    alt Confirmed commit
        GW-->>UI: 200 Task with revision
        UI-->>Member: Confirm result and renew permitted placement
    else Stale request rejected
        GW-->>UI: 409 Conflict
        UI-->>Member: Reload permitted state and reconsider
    else Response lost
        UI-->>Member: Outcome unknown - no fresh-key replay
    end
```

getTask is GET /tasks/{task_id}. setTaskState accepts todo/in_progress/done, not display labels. Reopening work from a Completed Sprint preserves completion history and returns it to Backlog in To Do; it does not reopen the Sprint. Member removal/rejoin never restores former restricted grants or delegated capabilities. Membership removal guards the last effective membership manager and invalidates grants/current assignees transactionally under existing policy.

#### 3.4.2 Buffered AI and document citation

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor Member
    participant UI as Drawer and inspector
    participant GW as Workspace gateway
    participant KN as Knowledge
    Member->>UI: Submit one question
    UI->>GW: POST /knowledge/questions
    GW->>KN: Authenticated scoped question
    Note over GW,KN: Persist exact manifests and validate whole evidence set before guarded delivery
    KN-->>GW: Validated result or declared failure
    GW-->>UI: Buffered permitted result or error
    Member->>UI: Open document citation
    UI->>GW: GET /knowledge/citations/{document_id}/{version_id}/{passage_id}
    GW->>KN: Renew current scope for exact locator
    KN-->>GW: Permitted passage or declared error
    GW-->>UI: Passage/version or generic error
```

Before provider input and answer delivery, server guards check the entire evidence set including uncited context, exact committed manifests/bytes, current access and validity. Invalid/revoked evidence withholds the original draft; removing chips/sentences is insufficient. Client validation cannot replace these checks. getVersion is a separate exact-version read; never substitute Current or invented offsets. Verified unavailable identity requires ADR-0013's surviving read policy, exposes no excerpt, and otherwise returns the same generic 404.

#### 3.4.3 Operational observation

Preserve delivered operational locator/time/revision only as ephemeral answer context. Renew getProject/getSprint/getTask to show permitted current state with a separate label. Reload/direct navigation without that context shows **Original observation unavailable**. URL/current values/browser storage cannot recreate authoritative history; no saved-answer/status endpoint is added.

Unknown and inaccessible reads return identical 404 `{"code":"not_found","message":"Resource unavailable"}`. Do not distinguish hidden existence or revocation cause. Clear protected output on expiry, denial or unknown authority; authority/dependency failure is not empty success. Already delivered information cannot be recalled. A 403 action denial is applicable only where the contract permits it for a known readable resource; never use it to distinguish an inaccessible read.

### 3.5 Information view

| State | Lifetime / constraints |
| --- | --- |
| Authenticated session | Mechanism remains OD-09; server identity authoritative; clear protected display/actions on sign-out/expiry/lost scope |
| Route/filter selectors | URLs select resources/views, never confer authority or reconstruct observations |
| Safe user-entered drafts | Ephemeral local form state; never refill protected old content after revocation |
| Preconditions | Opaque precondition_token binds actor/session/project/action/document/known version; consumed on commit, grants neither read nor action authority |
| Answer/observation | Ephemeral view memory only; no persisted answer/history feature |
| Operation identity | Preserve original scoped key/payload for reconciliation where available; lost context leaves explicit uncertainty |

| Operation | Exact wire constraints |
| --- | --- |
| createTask | Required type=story/task/bug and nonempty title; optional description. No priority field, UUID requirement or invented length maximum; use setAssignee separately. |
| setTaskState | state=todo/in_progress/done and numeric expected_revision, with scoped Idempotency-Key |
| reorderBacklog | Full unique task_ids and decimal-string expected_revision; ReorderResult returns project_id/backlog_revision |
| reviseDocument | content and content_format=text/markdown; exactly one known numeric expected_revision or matching precondition_token. Minimal 201 DocumentMutationReceipt, not content-bearing Version. |
| archive/delete | Already-known exact version for archive; lifecycle authority separate from manage-access/read. Receipt or delete 204 grants no content-read. |

OpenAPI controls required fields, additionalProperties, headers, exact error unions and bounds. Non-reading commands cannot prefill hidden title/content/history/current pointer; acquire only the selected action's precondition. After 409 reconsider the command with renewed permitted data/preconditions. Timeout is unknown, not proof of rollback; preserve the original identity/payload rather than obtain a fresh token/key and blindly resubmit.

### 3.6 Interface view

#### 3.6.1 Candidate tokens

Preserved from v1.1 as WF-09 design input only. This selects no framework/library/icon package or accepted device target. Contrast, rendering, timing and accessibility measurements are **Not run**. Former numerical contrast claims were unsupported and are withdrawn. Font size/line-height pairs are notation to translate into valid CSS, not an implemented stylesheet.

#### 3.6.2 Screen/route bindings

Pagination must never reveal hidden totals or counts.

### 3.7 State dynamics view

#### 3.7.1 AI results

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Loading: Deliberate submit
    Loading --> Answered: HTTP 200 answered
    Loading --> Partial: HTTP 200 partially_answered
    Loading --> Insufficient: HTTP 200 insufficient_evidence
    Loading --> Conflict: HTTP 200 conflict
    Loading --> Withheld: HTTP 503 answer_withheld
    Loading --> DependencyFailure: Declared dependency error
    Loading --> UnknownOutcome: Response lost or timeout
    Withheld --> Idle: Deliberate new question
    DependencyFailure --> Idle: Deliberate retry
    UnknownOutcome --> Idle: Explicit new intent subject to server quarantine
```

Partial contains supported claims/citations and explicit missing_components without hidden-source hints. Conflict is a 200 answer category, distinct from stale mutation 409. Withheld contains exactly code answer_withheld and message Unable to provide this answer; no generated text, run/source IDs or detailed cause. Other declared failures contain no draft. No automatic resend after unknown responses; new user intent cannot override server quarantine. A stale health badge cannot permanently disable the editor. Closing citation inspection restores its original result category/focus.

#### 3.7.2 Version lifecycle

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Current: First save commits
    Current --> Superseded: New immutable Current revision commits atomically
    Current --> Archived: Authorised archive
    Superseded --> Archived: Authorised archive
```

This models one immutable version; revision creates a different Current version and preserves old locators. No product Draft, publish or restore operation exists. Document deletion is independently authorised and does not require an already Archived version. Exact unavailable-locator policy follows ADR-0013; physical retention remains OD-04. Semantic readiness pending/ready/failed is orthogonal. Ordinary retrieval uses permitted Current; history is explicit and labelled.

### 3.8 Algorithm view

#### 3.8.1 Full Backlog reorder (Proposed ADR-0018)

1. Gather all listTasks(location=backlog) pages through next_cursor=null at one backlog_revision string. Reject filtered subsets; paging 409 discards the accumulated generation.
2. Enable reorder only when complete and current scoped discovery includes reorderBacklog. Check equal length, uniqueness and exact set equality locally; server remains authoritative.
3. Preserve scoped Idempotency-Key and payload `{task_ids: fullPermutation, expected_revision: capturedBacklogRevision}`. POST /projects/{project_id}/backlog-order.
4. On 200 acknowledge ReorderResult then renew permitted current state. A replay receipt may describe an earlier commit; response.backlog_revision is not proof of the current snapshot. Never assume +1.
5. On 409 discard stale pages/order, reload and require reconsideration. No automatic reapplication.
6. On lost response show Outcome unknown; reconcile the same original key/payload if available. No fresh-key blind retry, inferred rollback or invented status endpoint. Lost context retains uncertainty.
7. Clear protected rows/actions on expiry, denial or unknown authority. Dependency failure differs from empty success. WF-02/BL-01–10 specify frame variants.

#### 3.8.2 Metrics

For each permitted metric independently: measured zero renders 0 ms/0 tokens; unavailable renders Not measured; not_performed renders Not performed. Preserve each metric's actual unit and stage/status. Failed execution may have measured duration. Scope/dependency failure clears protected output and renders generic failure, not empty success or zero. Do not expose hidden rank gaps/counts; structure validation does not establish claim support (Proposed ADR-0021).

## Common interaction rules

Loading must not show cached protected content before renewed checks. Successful empty results differ from unavailable dependencies; never use an empty result to disguise failed authority. Unknown and denied protected resources have the same generic message and no hidden counts. Session expiry requires sign-in; detected membership loss clears protected view and cancels further protected requests. Already delivered information cannot be recalled.

Distinguish validation, confirmed rejection, committed success and unknown commit outcome. Keep user input when safe, but do not repopulate revoked source content from a browser cache. A lost mutation response is reconciled with the same key/payload before a new submission; optimistic display is never evidence of commit. Show the latest permitted state after conflict and let the user reconsider the intended edit. No automatic overwrite or blanket fresh-key retry.

AI outage leaves healthy work, documents and keyword paths usable. Knowledge outage also affects document search/reads; it does not imply Workspace task search or Board is unavailable. Show dependency-specific feedback. Do not permanently disable question retry from an obsolete global health badge; actual request outcomes remain authoritative.

Use native labelled controls, logical focus order, visible focus, text as well as color for status, inline errors associated with fields and keyboard alternatives to drag. On opening an inspector/dialog, place focus meaningfully and return it to the trigger when closing; avoid focus traps. Announce confirmed updates and errors without exposing hidden metadata. These are interaction design requirements to test, not a WCAG conformance claim. Device/browser targets and visual tokens remain design inputs, not invented fixed metrics.

Verify each listed state through real flows and inspect the rendered diagrams; structural lint alone cannot check legibility, route geometry or accessibility. Browser/device targets, delegated non-read capabilities and visual design choices require clarification when implementing affected flows. Optional task keyword search follows the separately owner-confirmed Should extension, not an automatic Must increase. No Figma publication, external transfer or generated user-research result occurred.

## Priority 2 screen-to-operation handoff — 18 October 2026

| Screen/control | Draft source | Required failure handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Membership management and assignment/owner/grantee selectors | listMembers; selected Member.revision for removal; known registered ID for adding a nonmember | Distinguish empty/error, restart stale pages, clear membership loss; manage controls require action authority |
| Explorer | listDocuments with permitted metadata and nullable Current pointer | Omit unreadable documents, include archived-only/readiness-failed sources; no hidden counts |
| Explicit history | listVersions; exact getVersion; document_revision | Label historical state; no substitution; restart changed pages |
| Known-ID manage route | getDocumentPolicy + listDocumentReadGrants; permission_revision | Permit independently scoped managers without content prefill; reload on stale policy |
| Scoped controls | getAllowedActions at global/project/exact resource scope | Missing action means disabled/hidden; authority failure clears old allows; actual mutation rechecks authority and business preconditions |

These projections address UX-R01/R02 drafting gaps under Proposed ADR-0019. Runtime acceptance and additional delegation remain open. Proposed ADR-0022 now supplies non-reading command preconditions; handler/token verification remains pending. No role editor, global user directory or new business capability is implied.

## Priority 2 recheck consumer correction

Version action discovery supplies project_id + document_id + version_id from the exact history row and verifies the echoed pair; resource_id is unused for that scope. Summary and trace controls use independent allowed operations for the same run: answer-reader entitlement enables optional FR-27 summary without trace-read, while FR-58 requires trace-read and does not inherit summary rights. No role or sibling document can fill a missing authority result. Proposed ADR-0019 v0.2 and SP-07/SP-13 carry the paired scenarios; UI/runtime acceptance is unrun.

## NEXT-03 trace/summary rendering contract

Inspection uses Knowledge v0.2.7 Trace/RetrievalSummary. Show actual permitted queries and recorded stage/status, exact document/operational identity and source-to-step ranks; operational observation time/revision is labelled historical. Trace has separately permitted configuration/duration/usage; optional summary contains only retrieval/citation stages. Do not invent a source-ID resolver or display hidden totals/gaps. Query state unavailable has no source-specific explanation. Validation locator success is distinct from claim-support evaluation.

Metric states render independently: measured zero is “0 ms” or “0 tokens”; unavailable is “Not measured”; not_performed is “Not performed”. Failed execution may still have measured timing. Scope/dependency failure clears protected output and uses generic failure, not zero metrics or empty success. Source opening rechecks exact current access. Proposed ADR-0021 and TC-11/18 define future tests; no rendered UI or runtime evidence is supplied here.

## NEXT-04 citation, retry and readiness bindings

Citation chips branch by kind. Document chips use exact openCitation/getVersion locators; operational chips show their recorded observation time/revision and separately refresh getProject/getSprint/getTask, never invent a document locator or historical snapshot. Current entity reads remain renewed permission checks.

After terminal AI failure/withholding, deliberate retry starts a fresh user request while preserving whole-draft withholding. Lost responses are labelled unknown and never replay automatically; an explicit new-question action does not override transport quarantine. A stale health badge cannot permanently lock the prompt. Readiness.semantic_readiness is semantic processing only; actual keyword availability is independent. TC-08/10/20/22 carry the unrun UI/runtime assertions.

## NEXT-05 current source and route inventory

The Sources and authority paragraph now identifies the current source editions. The sitemap main route table includes independent known-ID manage/actions routes and the operational observation inspector; document and operational inspectors use distinct existing HTTP reads. Descriptive member roles do not supply action authority. UI sources remain drafts; current version reconciliation is not a fresh usability/permission test. Proposed ADR-0022 supplies the non-reading concurrency/acknowledgement design; application evidence remains open.

## NEXT-06 command route handoff

The independent /docs/:docId/actions route now has a complete draft precondition/acknowledgement source: getDocumentCommandPrecondition for the selected action, opaque token submission and DocumentMutationReceipt (delete 204). It does not require content prefill or disclose a private current revision/state. Archive requires an already-known exact version; no history is inferred. A reader can fetch protected display state separately; no read grant follows from command success. Conflict requires reconsideration and unknown outcomes preserve the original operation identity. Proposed ADR-0022 resolves the design gap; all application evidence remains pending.

## NEXT-09 operational inspector recovery

The observation route has only current entity selectors. A reload/direct visit without the delivered citation context shows original observation unavailable; any renewed permitted current read is labelled separately. No timestamp, observation revision or historical value is inferred from current data, URL arguments or persistent browser state. No saved answer/history endpoint or extra entitlement is added. TC-08 specifies the future browser/revocation checks. The companion checklist report records this design omission and its bounded correction.

## Next wireframe work plan

[UX-PLAN-01](../ux/wireframe-workplan.md) orders the next Core design slices and supplies ten Backlog-reorder and ten independent-document-command state variants, plus AI/inspection distinctions. It selects no visual framework, design tool, device budget or new product feature. All rendered WF tasks remain unchecked; it is a textual handoff alongside the canonical sources, not evidence that UI has been implemented or validated.

## Input metadata reconciliation — 25 October 2026

Only input-version metadata is synchronized for the bounded architecture/UC/checklist corrections. Requirements, acceptance assertions, design body and prior observations are unchanged; no complete semantic review or runtime check is implied.

# Core wireframe work plan and semantic state brief

**Artifact ID:** UX-PLAN-01  
**Version/date:** 0.4 Draft · 1 November 2026\
**Status:** Planning/textual interaction brief; initial native frames and previews exist, while full WF acceptance and usability/runtime evidence remain open.\
**Inputs:** PRD-01 v0.9; UC-02 v0.8; SAD-03 v0.16; API-05 v0.22; UX-06 v0.13; UX-CHECK-01 v0.2; UX-HANDOFF-01 v0.9; current sitemap/permission/flow drafts.\
**Trace:** BR-01–BR-14; SC-01–SC-08; NFR-01–NFR-04; U03–U18/U20–U23 and B19 in the detailed checklist review.

## Scope and order

This brief turns the reviewed contract/flow gaps into bounded wireframe tasks. Checkboxes below track **future design outputs**, not application readiness. The correction queue separately tracks the delivery of this plan. Each task must include readable, loading, empty, denied, dependency-failure, conflict and unknown-outcome variants where applicable; omit a state only with its reason. Use synthetic content and exact operation bindings, without implying tested users or implemented APIs.

| Future task | Frames / purpose | Contract sources and acceptance for the design draft |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ ] WF-01 | Sign-in, project directory, current-member selectors and management entry | getSession/listProjects/getProject/listMembers/getAllowedActions; show empty versus failed lists, session expiry and read-only action variants. Management is capability-scoped; no global user directory or role-permission editor. |
| [ ] WF-02 | Backlog, Sprint selector/planning and multi-select allocation | listTasks/listSprints/listSprintItems/getSprint; show complete-versus-partial Backlog, task location independent of history, per-task confirmed/rejected/unknown allocation results and fixed Sprint lifecycle. |
| [ ] WF-03 | Three-column Board, task detail, assignee and ordered blocker history | getTask/listBlockerEvents plus mutation-specific allowed operations; keyboard state-change alternative, direct transitions, filtered-empty versus no-Active-Sprint, completion/reopen location and race/conflict feedback. |
| [ ] WF-04 | Read-filtered Docs explorer, exact version, history and semantic readiness | listDocuments/getDocument/listVersions/getVersion/getReadiness; Current/Superseded/Archived and semantic status are separate. No product Draft/publish/restore or blanket restricted-content access. |
| [ ] WF-05 | Known-ID access manager and independent non-reading commands | getDocumentPolicy/listDocumentReadGrants/getAllowedActions/getDocumentCommandPrecondition; show read/write/lifecycle/manage separation, action-bound concurrency and minimal acknowledgements. No hidden title/history/current pointer prefill. |
| [ ] WF-06 | Keyword search and explicit task/document relationships | keywordSearch/listLinks/openCitation as appropriate; separate document/task types, permitted endpoints and pagination errors. Task search is FR-70 Should and appears only if implemented/allowed; no hidden relationship counts. |
| [ ] WF-07 | Buffered AI, both citation kinds and deliberate recovery | askQuestion/openCitation/getVersion/getProject/getSprint/getTask; all answer/error states, exact historical/current labels and missing original observation context. No streamed unvalidated draft, saved-answer/status API or automatic resend. |
| [ ] WF-08 | Scoped audit, trace and optional retrieval summary | listAudit/getTrace/getRetrievalSummary; independent entitlements, permitted rows/query/steps/exact sources, honest missing metrics and separate generic dependency/authority errors. FR-27 summary remains Should. |
| [ ] WF-09 | Shared visual/components and interaction validation | Define proposed grid/tokens/type/icons and target viewports explicitly; then inspect contrast, touch/keyboard/focus, wrapping, overflow, destructive confirmations, loading/error/disabled states and task navigation on actual rendered drafts. No numeric/template target is accepted by this plan. |

Draft work and document frames before AI frames so fallback is a real journey. WF-09 starts with the first rendered drafts and continues across them; it is not a final cosmetic step. Record visual/device assumptions and unresolved owner inputs; do not claim inaccessible work is blocked only by a missing colour palette. No calendar estimate or completion-time target is supplied without a measured basis.

## Backlog reorder component — required frame variants

| State ID | Trigger and visible state | Action/next state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BL-01 | Initial list loading; no confirmed data | Show loading and no cached protected rows before renewed scope. |
| BL-02 | Permitted page(s), more pages remain | Readable rows may show; reorder controls remain disabled. A page/search subset cannot be submitted as the complete Backlog. |
| BL-03 | All pages loaded through next_cursor=null with one backlog_revision | Enable reorder only with current returned reorderBacklog action. Preserve revision as an exact string from these reads. |
| BL-04 | Complete permitted empty Backlog | Show empty guidance with capability-gated create/planning entries; no empty drag interaction. |
| BL-05 | Locally reordered complete list | Provide keyboard and pointer alternatives; submit the full permutation and its captured Backlog revision. No task/project revision substitution. |
| BL-06 | Mutation in flight | Show pending; avoid duplicate submission. Closing/cancelling the view does not prove rollback of server work. |
| BL-07 | Confirmed receipt | Refresh permitted current work; a replay receipt can describe an earlier commit. Do not treat a receipt as a current global snapshot. |
| BL-08 | 409 while paging or submitting | Discard the affected accumulated list, reload and require reconsideration. Do not merge generations or silently reapply an old order. |
| BL-09 | Lost mutation response | Show outcome unknown; reconcile the same original operation identity/payload when available. No fresh-key retry or inferred rollback. If that context is unavailable, keep the uncertainty explicit rather than inventing a request-status read. |
| BL-10 | Session/access/authority/dependency failure | Clear protected data on expiry/denial/unknown authority. Distinguish generic failure from an empty successful list. Healthy non-AI work is not disabled by an AI badge. |

The frames specify interaction; actual full-list membership, revision, capability and transaction checks remain server responsibilities. Multiple independent lists are not one atomic snapshot.

## Independent document action component — required frame variants

| State ID | Trigger and visible state | Action/next state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DC-01 | Known document ID, action discovery loading | No title/content/history/owner prefill unless independently readable. A known ID is not authority. |
| DC-02 | Exact scope permits a content/lifecycle action | Show only the corresponding control; manage-access alone does not enable it. The server still checks current authority at execution. |
| DC-03 | Revise without content-read | Accept new user-entered text; do not fetch or reconstruct protected old text. Explain immediate Current revision and absence of a publish step. |
| DC-04 | Archive selected | Require an already-known exact document/version target. Do not offer an implicit “archive current” lookup of a hidden version. |
| DC-05 | Obtaining command precondition | Request the selected action's opaque token. Token issuance shows no numeric revision/current pointer/lifecycle/content. |
| DC-06 | Ready to submit | Use exactly one already-known numeric expected revision or matching opaque token, plus original scoped idempotency identity. Token possession is not read/action authority. |
| DC-07 | Confirmed revise/archive/metadata receipt or delete 204 | Acknowledge only the command/new-or-supplied identity. Stay on the independent action surface; open protected display data only after separate renewed read checks. Do not infer a read grant from success. |
| DC-08 | Conflict/rejected precondition | Explain the need to reconsider; refresh only permitted state/preconditions. Never overwrite or silently replay the original edit. |
| DC-09 | Unknown result | Preserve original identity/payload when available; a newly issued token is not proof the previous command rolled back. No blind resubmit/new-key retry, invented polling endpoint or promise of automatic recovery after lost context. |
| DC-10 | Scope removed/unknown or service failure | Clear stale allowed actions/tokens/protected display. Use the existing generic denial/failure rules without hidden-content or revocation-cause hints. |

Visual layouts must distinguish membership management, document access management, content-read, content-write and lifecycle authority. Initial descriptive Member.role does not provision those capabilities. Additional delegation and account provisioning remain owner decisions.

## AI and inspector distinctions to retain in every frame

1. Loading/validation, answered, partially_answered, insufficient_evidence, conflict, terminal withheld and dependency failure are visibly distinct. Partial answers list supported citations and request-visible missing components; failures contain no generated answer or hidden-source hints.
2. A stale health badge does not permanently disable the editor. After a terminal failure, retry is deliberate new user intent with renewed scope; a lost response remains unknown and is never transparently resent. Server quarantine can still reject a new request.
3. Document inspection uses the exact document/version/passage and renewed access. Verified surviving unavailable identity differs from generic unknown/inaccessible; no excerpt or newer-version substitution.
4. Operational inspection separates the delivered observation locator/time from renewed current entity state. Reload/direct navigation without the original answer context shows original observation unavailable; URL/current values/browser storage cannot recreate authoritative history.
5. Measured zero displays as zero; unavailable as Not measured; unexecuted as Not performed. Summary, trace and audit are separate entitlements even when frames share a layout.
6. Provider outage, Knowledge outage and authority failure have different surviving paths. Work/docs/keyword usability follows their own healthy dependencies; no unrestricted cached fallback.

## Design handoff and evidence still required

For each WF task, supply the named frame variants, source operations, requirement/UC/TC links, assumptions and observed problems. Test keyboard/focus and synthetic user tasks on rendered output before claiming accessibility/usability. Use native labelled controls, visible focus and text for status; a modal must contain focus without stranding the user and restore it meaningfully on close. Measurements, browser/device choices, actual source support and owner policy require their own evidence.

No frame or UI feature is completed by this plan. Server handlers/current-authority, token storage, active process fence/guard/provider/transport, full API semantics and real UI/application acceptance remain open. This is a bounded next-work brief under the existing Core scope, not a UI framework/design-tool choice, new role policy, runtime AI write capability, external publication or scope deferral.

Checklist: Pass for ordered tasks, concrete Backlog/document command state variants and preserved Core distinctions; Gap for every unchecked rendered-design task and runtime gate. Handoff: use WF-01/WF-02 as the first design slices while retaining the documented assumptions and original 60 Must requirements.

## Initial visual artifacts and remaining acceptance — 25 October 2026

[UX-WF-EX-01](wireframes/README.md) supplies an editable scene and initial frame previews. This work plan still lacks complete acceptance evidence for the listed WF tasks, so its checkboxes remain unchecked. Artifact existence does not establish complete state variants, native Excalidraw rendering, responsive/accessibility/usability or runtime acceptance.

## P10 input metadata — 28 October 2026

Input versions synchronize the bounded session lifecycle update. Existing requirement, evaluation and UI assertions remain unchanged; no runtime acceptance is inferred from this metadata revision.

## Interaction and disclosure notes

Sign-in has no protected project navigation or data. After authentication, controls in the populated layouts assume the exact action is currently allowed; side navigation and controls must be omitted or disabled when the corresponding authority is absent. A role label grants nothing. Global header search/AI are project scoped. Sign out and session-expiry clearing remain specified in UX-06; the account-menu expansion is not drawn here.

Board states are To Do / In Progress / Done. A state selector is the keyboard alternative to drag. Backlog reordering requires the complete consistent list and current allowed action. Sprint completion retains Done items; unfinished work and reopened Completed-Sprint work return to Backlog as To Do. Allocation results are per task. Uncertain mutation results are not failure or rollback: preserve original operation context and reconcile it, never blindly resubmit with a new identity. No new polling/status endpoint is implied.

Document versions are Current / Superseded / Archived; semantic readiness is independent. Content revision is immediately Current, with no product Draft/publish. The independent management panel deliberately has no hidden title/content. Independent writing without read starts blank. Archive uses an already-known exact version; successful commands do not grant content access. Proposed ADR-0022's command-precondition protocol remains a design dependency; token issuance and all DC-01–10 substeps are not individually drawn.

The assistant is read-only. Answer preparation is buffered. Facts, synthesis and uncertainty are visibly separated. Both citation kinds are drawn: exact document/version/passage and operational revision/observation time with a separate current-state refresh. Example source names, locators, text, people, dates and metrics are fictional, not retrieval evidence. Unavailable citations disclose retained identity only when current policy permits; denied/unknown reads use the generic message. Authority/service failures are not successful empty results. AI failure preserves healthy Board, document and keyword paths; Knowledge failure can still affect documents/search.

Audit-read, trace-read and optional answer-local summary are independent. Restricted audit content stays redacted even when actor/action/entity/time are permitted. Optional task search and summary remain Should. No saved chat, automated assignment, reporting dashboard, publish/restore flow or new role editor is added.

## Visual assumptions and checks

Proposed desktop artboards are 1280 × 900, arranged in reading order. Arial, light neutral panels and restrained blue selection are wireframe choices, not an adopted design system or device-support commitment. Status is expressed as text as well as colour. Focus order follows header, navigation, main content and inspector. Implementation must add visible focus, labelled controls, keyboard movement, contained dialog focus, close/return focus and appropriate announcements. Static scene links do not prove these behaviours.

Author checks: scene JSON parses; IDs are unique; 12 frames contain their elements; local link targets exist; element bounds stay within the assigned artboard. PNG overview, Board and AI detail were visually inspected for layout/readability. Repository context and documentation checks are recorded in the register after execution. These checks prove no handler, permission, persistence, source support or usability behaviour.

Checklist: Pass for an editable initial desktop scene, screen/trace inventory and explicit state families. Gap for native Excalidraw import verification, exhaustive individual BL/DC frame variants, mobile layouts, expanded account controls, interactive keyboard/focus, contrast measurement, touch targets, user study, independent visual review and runtime verification. Existing WF-01–09 work-plan checkboxes remain unchecked because this initial draft does not close their full acceptance criteria.

Handoff: review the visual structure and density, then refine individual task/permission/lifecycle flows against the current contracts. Keep Proposed mechanics labelled Proposed. No owner decision or application implementation is established by this scene.
